title: Velvety Fermented Malaysian Vegetable Stock Tagine
description: A rich and hearty, fermented, velvety dish featuring a creamy Malaysian vegetable stock, slow-cooked in a traditional Tajine clay pot. This recipe is a nostalgic tribute to the flavors of Malaysia, with a FODMAP-friendly twist.
instructions: Heat the fermented rice bran oil in a Tajine clay pot over medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 10 minutes. Add the curry paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant. Stir in the kecap manis and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes. Add the vegetable stock and bring to a simmer. Stir in the coconut cream and bring to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to low and let simmer for 10-15 minutes. Stir in the lime juice and chopped cilantro. Season with salt to taste. Serve hot over steamed vegetables or with steamed rice.
Transfer the Tajine pot to a preheated oven or tandoor at 300°F (150°C) for an additional 30 minutes to enhance the fermentation process and flavor.
Let the dish rest for 10-15 minutes before serving. This will allow the flavors to meld and the stock to thicken.
Adjust seasoning as needed before serving.
